knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{4-5y} & =21 \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{4-5y}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
4-5y=\operatorname{ln}⁡(21).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(21) \\ -5y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)-4 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)-4) \\ y & =\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(21)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡(21).$

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(\ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{4-5y}&=11 \\ \ln(e^{4-5y})&=\ln(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln(e^u)=u$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
4-5y=\ln(11).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4-5y&=\ln(11) \\ -5y&=\ln(11)-4 \\ y&=\frac{1}{-5}\left(\ln(11)-4\right) \\ y&=\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\ln(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\ln(11).$

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(\ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{4+5y}&=11 \\ \ln(e^{4+5y})&=\ln(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln(e^u)=u$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
4+5y=\ln(11).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4+5y&=\ln(11) \\ 5y&=\ln(11)-4 \\ y&=\frac{1}{5}\left(\ln(11)-4\right) \\ y&=-\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{5}\ln(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-\frac{4}{5}+\frac{1}{5}\ln(11).$

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(\ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{-4-5y}&=11 \\ \ln(e^{-4-5y})&=\ln(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln(e^u)=u$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
-4-5y=\ln(11).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4-5y&=\ln(11) \\ -5y&=\ln(11)+4 \\ y&=\frac{1}{-5}\left(\ln(11)+4\right) \\ y&=-\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\ln(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-\frac{4}{5}-\frac{1}{5}\ln(11).$

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using the Natural Logarithm

question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the natural logarithm $(\ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}e^{7y+9}&=30 \\ \ln(e^{7y+9})&=\ln(30)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\ln(e^u)=u$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
7y+9=\ln(30).
$$

Finally, we solve for $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}7y+9&=\ln(30) \\ 7y&=\ln(30)-9 \\ y&=\frac{1}{7}\left(\ln(30)-9\right) \\ y&=-\frac{9}{7}+\frac{1}{7}\ln(30)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y=-\frac{9}{7}+\frac{1}{7}\ln(30).$
